gpus.notes: Valve's living-room PC with a semi-custom AMD RDNA 3 GPU (28 compute units, comparable to the Radeon RX 7600M) and 8 GB of GDDR6, next to a 6-core Zen 4 CPU. Listed as a desktop because the GPU only ships inside this machine; Mesa reports it as "AMD Steam Machine (RADV NAVI33)". System RAM is upgradeable (two SO-DIMM slots), so it's recorded per run and each RAM setup is its own test bench.

identity.name: Legion Go S Z1 Extreme 16 GB

gpus.notes: Lenovo's Legion Go S (8APU1) with the Ryzen Z1 Extreme and 16 GB of soldered LPDDR5X-7500, sold with Windows 11 or SteamOS. The power range is the chip's configurable TDP; Lenovo doesn't publish the device's own.

identity.name: Legion Go S Z1 Extreme 32 GB

gpus.notes: Lenovo's Legion Go S (8APU1) with the Ryzen Z1 Extreme and 32 GB of soldered LPDDR5X-7500, sold with Windows 11 or SteamOS. The power range is the chip's configurable TDP; Lenovo doesn't publish the device's own.

The original Steam Deck (64 GB, 256 GB, and 512 GB storage models), with the 7 nm Aerith APU: Zen 2 4C/8T at 2.4-3.5 GHz and 8 RDNA 2 CUs at up to 1.6 GHz (1.6 TFLOPS FP32), and 16 GB of LPDDR5-5500 on four 32-bit channels. APU power spans 4-15 W. Storage size doesn't change the chip, so every LCD model is this one entry.

ONE-NETBOOK's 3-in-1 handheld with Intel's Arc G3 Extreme (Panther Lake, 14 cores) and its Arc B390 graphics (12 Xe3 cores, up to 2300 MHz), with 32 GB of LPDDR5X-8533. Default TDP 35 W, 80 W boost. The 24 GB model uses slower LPDDR5X-7467, so it would be its own entry. Specs come from a retailer and a review site, because the maker's and Intel's pages couldn't be read.
